newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

ACT Brumbies rugby union fly-half David Knox is heading to South Africa to play in the Currie Cup for Natal under a six-figure contract that allows him to return to Australia in mid-October, and earlier if he is required for Wallaby duties. However, Knoxis not preparing for a recall, and has slammed Australian selectors for his omission from the Test team. Page 36.

The Australian cricket team may miss out on making its mark at the historically-favourable Lord's, with rain looking to drown the second Test in the Ashes series against England into a draw. Australian Prime Minister John Howard was one of the disappointd 28,000 fans who attended one of the most over-subscribed first days in history. Page 36.

Australian sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Taylor defeated fellow Australian Cathy Freeman in the 200 metres event at the Helsinki Grand Prix yesterday. The race was Gainsford-Taylor's first outing of her international campaign, and she finished with a time o 22.75s. Page 34.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

News Limited's sports director Ian Frykberg last night outlined Super League's plan for peace with the Australian Rugby League, a plan rejected by ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker. The plan, which would see a united competition in 1998, was rejected over the question of who would administer the competition. Page 46.

Australian tennis player and 1987 Wimbledon champion Pat Cash yesterday edged closer to a singles berth in this year's Wimbledon tournament with a narrow win over American Steve Campbell 4-6, 6-2, 11-9 in the qualifying tournament at Roehampton on Wednesdy. Page 46.

The Australian soccer team defeated Tahiti 2-0 in a flat World Cup qualifier at Parramatta Stadium last night. The Australian effort was less than impressive, the only highlight being the performance of Ned Zelic, who along with Paul Trimboli scored a gol. Page 45.
THE AGE

Australian Football League club Essendon's star player James Hird's management are believed to be concerned over the contract negotiations for next year, and say the Brownlow medallist could be available to play for another club next season if Essendon donot come up with a reasonable agreement soon. Page D3.

Senior administrators from Australian Football League clubs West Coast and North Melbourne, Brian Cook and Greg Miller, have both indicated to the AFL through their 1998 fixture position submissions that their clubs are not in favour of the state-of-origi matches. Page D3.

Australian 500cc motor cycle champion Michael Doohan has delayed his retirement plans and will ride again in 1998. Doohan, who is well ahead on the table this season, said he does not feel he has done enough racing yet, and now has to decide who he will race with next season. Page D4.
THE HERALD SUN

Eight first-gamers have been named in the Victorian side for the Australian Football League state of origin game against South Australia. The selection of the players indicate the end of an era, as chairman of selectors Gerard Healy said the new look tea reflected the absence of champion players who had been regulars for the State. Page 120.

Former Fitzroy Australian Football League coach Mick Nunan, who left Fitzroy after the club announced its merger plans, said from Adelaide yesterday that he would be interested in coaching Melbourne next season following the sacking of Neil Balme. Page 11.

The time may have come for Melbourne Tigers basketball coach Lindsay Gaze to hand over the reins to his deputy Al Westover. Gaze is the general manager of the Victorian Basketball Association and is also a member of various other boards, and admits that e is finding it difficult to devote enough time to the club. Page 108.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian tennis player Jason Stoltenberg ousted sixth-seeded American Jim Courier from the Nottingham Open 4-6, 6-3, 6-2 yesterday, in a game that saw Courier struggle with the heavier balls that were introduced to slow down the grass court game. Page 12.

The French rugby union side may be quite a threat to Australia in their Test on Saturday night, as the French have lost only one match - their semi-final against South Africa in 1995 - in the southern hemisphere since a loss at Ballymore in 1990. Page 124

In a bid to end delayed negotiations over the televising of racing on pay-TV, the Victorian racing industry has called on New South Wales to forgo its insistence to charge subscription fees to punters. Victoria believes that New South Wales will be bette off after the privatisation of the TAB and will not depend on the fees. Page 118.
